title: Coresidence With Husband's Parents, Labor Supply, and Duration to First Birth
note: THE EXTENDED ARM'S CENTRAL RECORD, and the browser recovered its abstract while confirming Duke UP paywalls the full text. The abstract carries the finding that matters most to this chapter: correcting for endogeneity REVERSES the sign of co-residence on the timing of first birth. Naive estimates say co-residence accelerates childbearing; the corrected estimate says it delays it. This is the estimator-disagreement problem, not a study disagreement.
